# LUI Desktop Parity Notes

This document records UX/UI differences between the experimental native SDL/Metal desktop host and the web app on the same `refactor/lui` revision, plus the follow-up fixes verified in this branch.

Audit baseline: `refactor/lui` @ `a5dd20796628acacc0ac2467ffa31b8169b3ebaa` (`2026-11-26 01:15:38 +0800`).

## Scope and setup

- Web: `static/` served at `http://localhost:3010/`, Chrome with an isolated profile.
- Native: direct macOS SDL/Metal host `deps/ui/_build/default/ocaml_host/logseq_native.exe`, launched with isolated graph/UI-state roots, `LUI_GPU=metal`, and the matching native DB worker.
- Both menu paths were smoke-tested: the default native NSMenu path and `LOGSEQ_NATIVE_MENUS=0` overlay-menu path.
- Both windows were sized to approximately 1575x1080 during the initial comparison. Initial captures used light theme; later captures used dark theme after theme-switch testing.
- Fresh isolated graphs were used. No existing user graph was mutated. Exact content parity was impossible after interactive editing because the seeded text necessarily diverged.
- Setup artifact only: the first web boot failed because `static/js/db-worker.js` had not been built. After `pnpm db-worker:build`, the web app booted normally. This is not counted as a parity finding.
- Login and RTC were intentionally skipped in the follow-up pass.
- The LUI pin in this branch uses `210041742a859f8bc026566d9dd2a82f3f0da90e`, which includes the compatibility backports through [lui#418](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/418), the macOS video-audio transport from [lui#419](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/419), the audio-tail EOF correction from [lui#420](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/420), the anchored-tooltip lifecycle from [lui#422](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/422), the allocation-safe tooltip owner index from [lui#423](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/423), the opt-in textarea navigation-key bridge from [lui#424](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/424), structured multi-format clipboard transport from [lui#425](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/425), and the web direct-tooltip trigger correction from [lui#426](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/426).

## Intentional desktop differences

These differences are deliberate desktop-host behavior. They should not be counted as parity defects unless the product decision changes.

| Area | Native desktop behavior | Web behavior | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Navigation history controls | The native desktop header always mounts back/forward buttons, matching packaged desktop-app chrome. | Browser web hides these buttons because the browser already provides navigation chrome; the web implementation mounts them only for Electron. | Intentional |
| Native performance bar | The native desktop host shows a bottom performance bar with FPS availability and a metrics-dialog control. | The web app has no equivalent visible bottom performance bar. | Intentional |

| High | Native FPS and journal input latency | Software/Cocoa/GL presentation frames were not counted, Metal could remain at zero FPS, input latency samples were cleared before an input-driven frame painted, and asynchronous edit updates could wait for the next frame deadline. | The host now counts non-skipped surface presentations across backends, keeps input latency measurement until the dirty input frame is painted, and prioritizes pending-input frames instead of quantizing them to the frame deadline. | Pass: real SDL/Metal validation showed finite FPS and correct typing; measured input-to-presented-frame p95 improved from 17.6ms to 10.8ms without extra GPU submissions. |
| High | Native text clarity | Small journal text looked bloated/fuzzy because glyph coverage was composited without output-gamma correction and CoreText's light-ink coverage gain was also applied to near-black text. | Native scenes now correct text coverage for gamma-encoded window surfaces, and the LUI compatibility line limits manual coverage thickening to light ink ([lui#418](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/418)). | Pass: same-text 16px runtime comparison against Apple native CoreText reduced darkness-mass mismatch from +52.9% to +7.6%, with no chromatic fringing or missing glyphs. |
| High | Live resize presentation | Cocoa live resize starved SDL event delivery, so the host could composite stale stretched frames and transiently expose black edges, especially during vertical resize. | The macOS Metal path now repaints from the display-link live-resize callback while SDL is blocked in its runtime-lock-releasing wait, then rethrows any callback failure on the main loop. | Pass: real SDL/Metal validation showed continued GPU submissions at about 56-58/s during vertical/diagonal drags; no black-edge or stale-stretch regression reproduced on the test display. |

| High | View toolbar popup dismissal | Filter/sort/view-type/more popups closed and immediately reopened when their trigger was pressed again. | These anchored toolbar popups now opt into trigger toggling instead of unconditional reopen. | Pass: browser validation for all four triggers, outside dismissal, and item selection. |
| High | Popup/dialog/menu exit icons | Icons disappeared early or became black blocks while surfaces exited. | The merged LUI exit-icon retention backport is consumed through the compatibility pin ([lui#415](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/415)). | Pass: real SDL/Metal graph-menu and search-dialog exit frames retained icons without black blocks. |
| High | Query-builder anchored tooltips | Anchored tooltips painted permanently as empty inverse rectangles, leaving a persistent black `Set query` fragment and no readable label. | The LUI compatibility pin now includes [lui#422](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/422): anchored tooltips hide at rest, open after hover delay or immediately on keyboard focus, close after pointer leave/press/Escape, and paint inverse-surface text. | Pass: real SDL/Metal validation showed no tooltip at rest, readable `Set query` while hovered, and collapse to `0x0` after pointer leave. |
| High | Math/KaTeX rendering | Native math rendered as readable source text rather than typeset KaTeX. | Native now embeds KaTeX through the trusted QuickJS runtime, flattens KaTeX layout commands in OCaml, rasterizes text/rules/stretchy SVG art through the host image pipeline, and falls back to raw source only for invalid or out-of-bounds input. | Pass: real SDL/Metal validation showed inline `x^2` and centered display fraction/square-root math, click-to-edit raw TeX, Escape round-trip, invalid-input fallback, and web/native ink metrics within roughly 6%. |

Decode failure still lacks a native broken-image/alt fallback, and native ignores the lazy-loading hint. |

## Remaining confirmed gaps or architectural differences

| Severity | Area | Current native behavior | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medium | Accessibility tree | macOS accessibility inspection exposes only native window chrome and menu-bar items; application content is absent from the accessibility tree. | Confirmed architectural gap. No small parity patch was attempted. |
| Medium | Code editing | Code blocks expose the native plain-text editing path rather than web CodeMirror behavior; runtime smoke did not show CodeMirror chrome or syntax highlighting. | Confirmed architectural/capability difference, although the exact editing hit-test UX remains uncertain. |
| Medium | Query block layout | `/query` insertion, operator/filter completion, Apply, popup dismissal, and compact control geometry now match web closely; direct query-settings tooltips failed on web because the web backend resolved the trigger to inner icon content rather than the retained button. | Native tooltip behavior was fixed in [lui#422](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/422) and kept within the pointer-hit allocation budget in [lui#423](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/423); web direct-child trigger resolution is fixed in [lui#426](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/426). `task: Todo` still returns `No matched result` for a matching `TODO` block in both apps, so that is a shared query-semantics question rather than a native parity mismatch. |
| Medium | Structured block clipboard | Native now transports `text/plain`, `text/html`, and `application/logseq` through the OS clipboard and prefers the structured payload on paste. | Fixed for platform transport and validated on Linux/macOS, including cross-process macOS pasteboard reads. Linux restart persistence depends on the desktop clipboard manager: in the validation environment the owner exit removed all formats. Remaining editor-semantics follow-ups are mixed `th`/`td` first-row table behavior and structured paste inside comment drafts. |
| Medium | Block context-menu keyboard | Native now closes the menu on Tab, closes the current submenu/root layer on Shift+Tab, opens submenu rows with ArrowRight, and closes them with ArrowLeft while preserving ArrowDown/Enter/Escape behavior. | Fixed and validated in a real isolated Linux SDL host. Remaining gap: root-trigger focus restoration after Tab/Shift+Tab is not implemented because the native menu does not retain a trigger element. |
| Medium | Plugin runtime beyond opening the dialog | Native reports no installed plugins, toolbar items, palette commands, marketplace actions/settings, or plugin README support. | Source-confirmed capability gap. Opening the Plugins dialog itself is fixed. |
| Medium | Multi-window support | Native windows are process-isolated rather than multiple SDL windows inside one host process. All Graphs now exposes `Open in new window`, which launches another native host process with the target graph deep link; both windows share the per-graph db-worker daemon. Shared native preferences use a cross-process lock plus read-modify-write merge so concurrent windows do not overwrite each other's keys. Deleting a graph broadcasts `local-graph-gone` through the shared daemon so other attached windows remove that graph and navigate away instead of remaining editable. | Runtime pass on macOS: two native windows opened the same graph, edits from both windows appeared in the shared journal, closing one window left the other alive, and external HTTP links still used the system browser. Caveat: there is not yet a dedicated File → New Window menu command. |
| Medium | Sidebar typography | Native sidebar row spacing and left alignment are close to web; the earlier unresolved-size mismatch was fixed in this branch. Font rasterization is closer to Apple native rendering after the gamma/dark-ink coverage fixes, but native is still bitmap glyph compositing rather than platform text rendering. | Mostly fixed; residual platform-raster differences are uncertain. |
| Medium | Asset/media richness | PDF assets intentionally open a self-drawn native viewer on the left on macOS with PDFKit rendering, page navigation, zoom, scrolling, text highlights and area highlights. PDF popout windows are an intentional process-isolated multi-window design: the toolbar popout action opens a dedicated PDF process while the parent keeps its embedded viewer; closing or docking that popout returns to the parent. Multiple simultaneous PDF windows are intentional and share the graph daemon/master-compatible annotation data. Normal-clicking another PDF intentionally replaces the embedded PDF, while mod+click intentionally opens that PDF directly in a new window. On macOS the annotation menu uses a real AppKit `NSMenu`; Linux keeps the in-host fallback. Linux/Windows use the same viewer contract through a dynamically loaded PDFium adapter; the Linux x86_64 release bundles pinned PDFium `chromium/8179` and Linux runtime validation passed for loading, rendering, and selection geometry, while Windows full SDL-host runtime validation and packaging remain blocked by the missing native Windows host target. PNG upload and local image rendering now pass for PNG/PDF area captures, including proportional journal-width scaling; normal image assets now open a basic native lightbox, while PhotoSwipe multi-image navigation, pinch/zoom, and sharing chrome remain missing. PNG/GIF/BMP/PNM decode through the bundled cross-platform image decoder; JPEG decoding uses platform decoders on macOS and Linux. On macOS, WebP/HEIC/AVIF decode through the same native ImageIO pipeline when the installed operating system includes those codecs; HEIC/AVIF were validated on the macOS 15 test host, while older OS codec coverage remains unverified. Linux now decodes still WebP through runtime-loaded system libwebp and still AVIF/HEIC through runtime-loaded system libheif; animated WebP and Windows WebP/AVIF/HEIC remain unsupported. MP4/WAV upload plumbing copies files into isolated assets. Linux native audio/video assets now render owner-scoped controls backed by the platform media host: WAV/MP3 playback, pause, seek, and MP4/H.264 poster/frame playback passed isolated SDL validation. On macOS the same controls use LUI media playback/decoding: MP4 poster/frame playback, pause, resume, and seek passed isolated SDL/Metal validation, with synchronized audio-channel playback through the merged LUI video transport; audible output remains physically unverified on the headless validation host. MP4 startup can still take about 2–3 seconds in the headless PulseAudio validation VM, and PNG export/copy reports unsupported. | PDF viewer/annotation creation, placement, popout windows, macOS annotation menus, Linux PDFium validation, local image rendering, and native media playback improved in this branch; the Windows native host target/packaging/media backend, physical audible-output validation, animated WebP and image-sequence decoding, non-JPEG platform image decoders on Windows, and image export/copy remain gaps. |
| Medium | Custom CSS | Native custom-CSS functions are no-ops. | Source-confirmed capability gap. |
| Low | Markdown-to-HTML conversion | Native `markdown_to_html` returns input unchanged. | Source-confirmed capability gap; visual impact uncertain. |
| Low | Confirmation dialogs | Native `confirm` always returns false. | Source-confirmed capability gap; affected flows untested. |
| Low | Selection ranges | Native host `set-selection-range` only handles select-all-like ranges and ignores other ranges. | Source-confirmed implementation limitation; user impact uncertain. |
| Medium | Remote-image redirect/private-network policy | Web/Electron uses ordinary browser image loading with no Logseq-level private-network or redirect restriction. Native libcurl validates only the initial URL against its documented public-host policy, then follows redirects internally without revalidating each hop. | Security/product decision required. Strictly revalidating every redirect closes the bypass but diverges from web for LAN/private images; matching web improves parity but weakens the existing native security boundary. Do not implement until that tradeoff is decided. |
| Low | Online status | Native `online()` is hard-coded true. | Source-confirmed; runtime untested. |
| Low | Share/public URLs | Native has no public origin/pathname, so generated share URLs degrade to graph fragments. | Source-confirmed; user impact depends on host/share design. |
| Medium | Math/KaTeX fidelity | Native math is bitmap/raster output rather than browser text layout. Common inline/display math now matches web closely, but horizontal spacing for complex constructs can diverge, bitmap math is not selectable/copyable as text, click-to-edit caret placement cannot yet map bitmap coordinates back to exact source offsets, and unsupported or out-of-bounds input falls back to raw TeX. | Improved in this branch; residual renderer fidelity limitation. |
| Low | CSS animation/transform behavior | Native disables CSS-transform icons and CSS animations. | Source-confirmed platform limitation; specific visual impact uncertain. |
| Low | Comments | Native comments use raw textarea-style editing/input rather than the full editor surface; comment scrolling is stubbed. | Source-confirmed implementation difference; UX impact untested. |
| Low | Content layout details | Native uses simplified hard-coded padding/margins and bottom spacing; web uses CSS container classes and bottom padding. Wide-mode max-width behavior itself is fixed in this branch. | Source-confirmed implementation difference; residual visual impact only partially verified. |
| High | Embedded video playback | Web renders provider embeds through browser iframes; native now lays out the same embed shell/frame geometry but the SDL/Metal host has no iframe or webview surface, so iframe children are empty and YouTube/Vimeo/Bilibili/Loom playback is unavailable. | Confirmed architectural gap. A webview/media surface integration is required; shell sizing alone does not provide playback. |

## Additional runtime smoke results after the fixes

Passed:

- Shift-Tab outdent.
- Multi-block selection and selection toolbar.
- Plain multi-block copy/paste preserving nested structure.
- Block drag/drop, with one caveat that an end-drop attempt did not reorder before a second drop succeeded.
- Block zoom through bullet click.
- Cmd+Enter TODO cycling.
- Property picker/editing, with confusing intermediate commit/display feedback.
- `#Task` table opening and Status cell editing from `Doing` to `Done`.
- Direct Unicode rendering/input for `😀` and `中文` (this is not real IME composition proof).
- Default macOS NSMenu smoke, including `View → Toggle Left Sidebar`.
- `LOGSEQ_NATIVE_MENUS=0` overlay-menu smoke, including block context menu → `Open in sidebar`.
- Import SQLite picker plumbing through file selection; an intentionally invalid SQLite file reached the expected `Import failed` validation.
- Export EDN save-panel plumbing and file writing.

Uncertain or caveated:

- Keyboard-focus restoration after a macOS open panel: immediately after the picker closed, one automated typing attempt did not enter text even though the input looked focused; after explicitly clicking the input, typing worked. This is uncertain because automation timing may contribute.
- Property value commit/display feedback is confusing; the value eventually appeared, but the exact commit timing/gesture needs product-level UX review.
- Code-block hit testing/editing may be a UX issue beyond the known plain-text-vs-CodeMirror architecture difference.
- Search palette footer text may differ because tips are randomized per mount; do not treat the original footer-text difference as a defect without a controlled comparison.
- Page menu item differences (`Copy page URL`, publishing visibility) may be intentional host capability differences.
- Quick-add focus/draft edge case after closing Help while quick add was open remains low-confidence and convoluted.
- The export dialog still shows web-centric File System Access API text in native even though native save panels now work.
- The web run exposed a separate modal-close regression: after closing quick add with Escape, an inert/invisible layer appeared to intercept sidebar clicks until reload. This is a web issue, not a native parity gap.


Follow-up runtime results:

- Passed on Linux: MP4/H.264 poster/frame playback, WAV/MP3 playback, pause, and seek render through native media controls in an isolated graph. Remaining caveat: MP4 playback startup took about 2–3 seconds in the headless PulseAudio validation VM; the Windows platform backend remains unimplemented; macOS video plays visually through LUI media and its audio track is now routed through the merged AVPlayer-backed transport; physical audible output remains unverified on the headless validation host.
- Failed: custom CSS text entry accepted `body { background: red !important; }`, but no visual change occurred.
- Passed with caveat: block context-menu ArrowDown/Enter opened `Open in sidebar`. The later ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, Shift+Tab, and repeated-Tab failures in this bullet were historical pre-fix results; they are superseded by the fixed context-menu keyboard row above. Root-trigger focus restoration and deeper non-picker nested-list traversal remain gaps.
- Failed before later fixes: math remained raw `x^2` and calculator showed only a shell without evaluation; both results are superseded by the fixed rows above. The later macro matrix also superseded the initial `{{youtube abcdef12345}}` probe: macro parsing is shared, shell geometry/warning/icon visibility fixes are runtime-verified, but actual provider playback remains unavailable without an iframe/webview surface.
- Passed: fixed caret placement, quick-add autocomplete/slash layering, compact context menu, open panels, and save-panel presentation remained working in the follow-up run.
- Passed on macOS: Markdown directory import completed through the real native directory picker in an isolated graph. Imported journal/page content, nested blocks, page links, search results, and a copied image asset were visible; the copied asset exactly matched the fixture bytes. Caveat: immediately after the picker closed, the first automated graph-name typing did not land until the input was clicked, matching the existing focus-transition caveat.
- Linux structured clipboard root cause: same-process structured nested copy/paste passed; while the source app stayed alive, X11 exposed `text/plain`, `text/html`, and `application/logseq`; after the source exited, the clipboard owner disappeared and all formats became unavailable because the validation environment lacked clipboard-manager/SAVE_TARGETS persistence. This is an environment/platform-persistence limitation, not a structured-payload publication or paste-parsing failure.
- Linux table controls: native filter and grouping controls were exposed with the expected properties, but sorting direction, filter apply/clear, and actual grouping were not objectively validated because the automation fixture/input was unreliable. Treat these as partially tested rather than product failures.

## Surfaces that appeared parity-passing in runtime comparison

- Fresh journal home/startup layout, allowing for host chrome and intentional desktop deltas.
- Left sidebar open state, navigation sections, Favorites/Recent structure, graph selector menu.
- Search palette structure and Journal search results.
- Right-sidebar open state and Contents/Help tabs after the disclosure fix.
- Settings dialog structure, General and Editor panes, theme thumbnails, and dark-theme switching.
- Tag page/table rendering.
- All Pages and All Graphs tables/routes.
- Import surface/options.
- Empty Flashcards state.
- Help menu and Handbook content.
- Once a native editor was genuinely focused: ASCII typing, `é`, Enter/new block, Tab indent, Escape commit, undo, and redo.

## Surfaces not tested or only partially tested

- Real IME composition for Chinese/Japanese/Korean. Direct Unicode injection is not IME proof; the follow-up host environment only had ABC input enabled.
- Structured clipboard cut/paste and desktop-specific clipboard-manager persistence beyond the validated same-process/cross-process transport behavior.
- Advanced query editor and query semantics beyond the tested insertion, operator/filter completion, Apply, popup dismissal, and compact geometry. `task: Todo` matching remains uncertain because both apps returned `No matched result` for a matching TODO block.
- Image lightbox richness beyond basic open/close behavior; Linux validation before the native lightbox implementation showed PNG rendering passed but clicking only selected the block.
- Custom user macros and built-in macro matrix beyond the tested video embed, timestamp, deprecated-warning, unknown-warning, and cloze cases. Cloze toggling still has an uncertain first-click caveat. Actual embedded-provider playback remains unavailable in native pending an iframe/webview surface.
- Plugin marketplace installation/actions.
- RTC/synced-graph status and login flow (explicitly skipped).
- Full macOS native menu command coverage beyond smoke-tested commands.
- Directory import edge cases beyond the passing small Markdown fixture (large trees, invalid files, name collisions, and partial-import recovery).
- Table submenu pointer hover hysteresis and menu dismissal edge cases; core sorting, filtering, clearing, grouping, and ungrouping passed real macOS SDL/Metal validation on a deterministic multi-row fixture.
- Deeper non-picker nested-list context-menu traversal remains untested because the default native block menu exposes picker submenus.

## Evidence inventory

Runtime evidence is under `/tmp` because these are test artifacts rather than repository files:

- `/tmp/logseq-native-web-parity` — original paired audit report, screenshots, recording, and logs.
- `/tmp/logseq-native-fix-verify` — empty-block/caret/Plugins/Export dialog verification.
- `/tmp/logseq-native-fix-verify-overlay` — quick-add autocomplete and slash-menu layering verification.
- `/tmp/logseq-native-fix-verify-small` — context menu, disclosure, window-title verification.
- `/tmp/logseq-native-untested-smoke` — broad editing/menu/table smoke report and screenshots.
- `/tmp/logseq-native-fileops-verify2` — file picker/download verification, recording, screenshots, and exported EDN artifact.
- `/tmp/logseq-native-remaining-smoke` — partial asset/query smoke report, follow-up media/CSS/macro/sidebar report, annotated recording, screenshots, crash logs, and evidence archives.
- `/tmp/logseq-native-multiwindow` — process-isolated multi-window verification reports, recordings, screenshots, process evidence, and host logs.

- Native query-builder tooltips previously persisted as empty inverse rectangles because anchored tooltips had no host-managed visibility lifecycle and native tooltip chrome did not paint its own text. Fixed in [lui#422](https://github.com/logseq/lui/pull/422): anchored tooltips hide at rest, open on hover/focus delay, close after pointer leave/press/Escape, and paint readable text.
